Read the passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:
Alcohols are versatile compounds as they can act as both nucleophile and electrophile. They undergo reactions based on
cleavage of O-H and C-O bonds. The cleavage of O-H bond reflects the acidic character of alcohols. However they are weaker
acids than water, phenol and carboxylic acids. Alkoxide ion formed by loss of proton from the OH group of alcohols reacts with
water to form the corresponding conjugate acid - base pair. They act as Bronsted base due to presence of unshared electron
pairs on oxygen. Both alcohols and phenol react with carboxylic acids, acid chlorides and anhydrides to form esters. The
introduction of acetyl group in alcohols or phenol is known as acetylation. Alcohols react with hydrogen halides to form alkyl
halides which form the basis of Lucas test. They also undergo acid catalyzed dehydration to form alkenes. Aleohols can be easily
oxidized with variety of oxidizing agents. The nature of the product depends on the type of oxidizing agent and the nature of
alcohol.
Identify the most acidic alcohol among the following:
detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers (Acidity of Alcohols):
Butanol

Detailed Analysis:
Step 1: Compare structures of butanol (1°), isobutanol (1° with steric hindrance), tertiary butanol (3°), and isopropanol (2°). Step 2: 3° alcohols have maximum +I effect, least acidity. 1° (butanol) has least +I effect, highest acidity.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.
